lessons.title: Mhoro! — Hello!
lessons.description: Learn the essential Shona greetings used every day across Zimbabwe
culturalNotes: In Shona culture, greetings are sacred and show respect
Always greet before any conversation — skipping greetings is considered rude

vocabulary.usage: Response when speaking for a group

lessons.title: Ini Ndinonzi... — My Name Is...
lessons.description: Introduce yourself and ask others their names in Shona
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Ini Ndinonzi...
culturalNotes: Names in Shona culture carry deep meaning and often reflect circumstances of birth
It is polite to ask someone's name after greeting them

vocabulary.english: my name is / I am called

lessons.title: Hongu neKwete — Yes and No
lessons.description: Master essential response words and polite expressions in Shona
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Hongu neKwete
culturalNotes: Politeness is highly valued — always say ndatenda (thank you)
Pamusoroi is used both as 'excuse me' and to show sympathy

lessons.title: Chii? Sei? — What? How?
lessons.description: Learn question words to start asking about the world around you
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Chii? Sei?
culturalNotes: Asking questions shows interest and respect in Shona culture
Use 'ko' at the start of a sentence to make it a question

lessons.title: Mhuri Yangu — My Family
lessons.description: Learn the core family words that every Shona speaker uses daily
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Mhuri Yangu
culturalNotes: Family (mhuri) is the foundation of Shona society
Respect for elders is shown through language and behavior

vocabulary.usage: Also used respectfully for older men
Also used respectfully for older women
Brother (if you're female) or sister (if you're male)

lessons.title: Vanhu Vemhuri — Family Elders
lessons.description: Learn words for extended family members and elders
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Vanhu Vemhuri
culturalNotes: Extended family plays a huge role — uncles and aunts are like second parents
Sekuru and ambuya are deeply respected figures

lessons.title: Shamwari neMuvakidzani — Friends & Neighbors
lessons.description: Learn words for people in your social circle beyond family
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Shamwari neMuvakidzani
culturalNotes: Neighbors (muvakidzani) are treated almost like family
The Shona proverb says: Musha mukadzi — a home is the woman

lessons.title: Ini, Iwe, Isu — Me, You, Us
lessons.description: Master Shona pronouns to talk about yourself and others
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Ini, Iwe, Isu
culturalNotes: Using 'imi' instead of 'iwe' shows respect to elders
Pronouns change based on respect level — this is key to polite Shona

vocabulary.usage: Casual — for friends and younger people

lessons.title: Kuverenga 1-10 — Counting
lessons.description: Learn to count from 1 to 10 in Shona — essential for markets and daily life
culturalNotes: Numbers are vital at markets — you'll use them every day
Shona uses a base-10 counting system

lessons.title: Nhamba Huru — Big Numbers
lessons.description: Count beyond 10 — learn bigger numbers for money, age, and quantities
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Nhamba Huru
culturalNotes: Knowing big numbers is essential for handling money (mari)
Zimbabwe uses both Shona and English numbers in daily life

lessons.title: Nguva — Time
lessons.description: Talk about times of day, today, tomorrow, and yesterday
culturalNotes: Greetings change based on time of day
Mangwanani is both 'morning' and the morning greeting

lessons.title: Mazuva — Days & Seasons
lessons.description: Learn the days of the week and seasons of the year in Shona
culturalNotes: Shona days of the week are derived from counting
Agricultural seasons deeply influence Shona life and language

lessons.title: Zvokudya — Food
lessons.description: Learn the names of common Zimbabwean foods and drinks
culturalNotes: Sadza (thick maize porridge) is the staple food of Zimbabwe
Meals are often communal — eating together strengthens bonds

lessons.title: Kumba — At Home
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary for things around the home
culturalNotes: The home (musha) is central to Shona identity
Traditional homes have separate kitchen huts (dare)

lessons.title: Muviri Wangu — My Body
lessons.description: Learn the names of body parts — useful for health and descriptions
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Muviri Wangu
culturalNotes: Knowing body parts helps when visiting a chiremba (doctor)
The heart (moyo) is considered the seat of emotions in Shona culture

lessons.title: Mavara — Colors
lessons.description: Learn color words to describe the vibrant world around you
culturalNotes: Colors carry symbolic meaning in Shona culture
The Zimbabwe flag colors each represent something important

lessons.title: Kumusika — At the Market
lessons.description: Learn essential words for shopping at Zimbabwean markets
culturalNotes: Markets (musika) are vibrant social spaces
Bargaining is expected and part of the fun

lessons.title: Kufamba — Getting Around
lessons.description: Learn transport and direction words for navigating Zimbabwe
culturalNotes: Kombis (minibuses) are the main public transport in cities
Walking is very common in rural areas

lessons.title: Mabasa — At Work
lessons.description: Learn common occupations and workplace vocabulary
culturalNotes: Respect titles are important — always address professionals properly
Teaching and farming are highly respected professions

lessons.title: Kudya Panze — Eating Out
lessons.description: Learn phrases for ordering food and drinks when eating out
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Kudya Panze
culturalNotes: Sharing food is a sign of friendship and hospitality
Tea (tii) is very popular in Zimbabwe, often with lots of sugar

lessons.title: Zvandinoita — What I Do
lessons.description: Learn the most common action verbs used in everyday Shona
culturalNotes: Shona verbs start with 'ku-' in their infinitive form
The verb prefix changes based on who is doing the action

lessons.title: Basa Repamba — Housework
lessons.description: Learn verbs for daily household activities
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Basa Repamba
culturalNotes: Housework is often shared among family members
Cooking (kubika) is a valued skill taught from childhood

lessons.title: Kudzidza — Learning
lessons.description: Learn words related to school and education
culturalNotes: Education is highly valued in Zimbabwean culture
Zimbabwe has one of the highest literacy rates in Africa

lessons.title: Kutaura — Communicating
lessons.description: Learn verbs for communication and perception
culturalNotes: Oral tradition is central to Shona culture — speaking and listening are deeply valued
Storytelling (ngano) passes wisdom between generations

lessons.title: Manzwiro — Feelings
lessons.description: Express your emotions and ask others how they feel
culturalNotes: Emotions are often expressed through proverbs rather than directly
Community support during hard times is a core value

lessons.title: Ndinofunga Kuti — I Think That
lessons.description: Learn to express opinions and agree or disagree
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Ndinofunga Kuti
culturalNotes: Respectful disagreement is important — use softening words
Elders' opinions carry extra weight in Shona culture

lessons.title: Ndine Urombo — I'm Sorry
lessons.description: Master polite expressions for apologies and deep gratitude
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Ndine Urombo
culturalNotes: Apologizing properly is important for maintaining relationships
Saying 'ndinotenda zvikuru' (I am very grateful) shows deep respect

lessons.title: Zvizhinji! — Expressions
lessons.description: Learn common everyday expressions that make your Shona natural
culturalNotes: These expressions are used constantly in daily conversation
Using them will make you sound more natural

lessons.title: Tsika — Traditions
lessons.description: Learn about core Shona cultural practices and customs
culturalNotes: Tsika (traditions) guide social behavior and relationships
Respecting elders and ancestors is fundamental to Shona life

lessons.title: Tsumo — Proverbs
lessons.description: Learn famous Shona proverbs that carry deep wisdom
culturalNotes: Proverbs (tsumo) are central to Shona oral tradition
Using proverbs in speech shows wisdom and education

lessons.title: Mbira neNgoma — Music & Art
lessons.description: Explore the rich musical and artistic traditions of Zimbabwe
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Mbira neNgoma
culturalNotes: The mbira is considered a sacred instrument that connects the living to ancestors
Music and dance are inseparable in Shona culture

lessons.title: Mwari naMadzinza — Spirituality
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary related to Shona spiritual and religious life
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Mwari naMadzinza
culturalNotes: Most Zimbabweans blend traditional beliefs with Christianity
Mwari (God) is recognized in both traditional and Christian contexts

lessons.title: Mhuka — Animals
lessons.description: Learn the names of common animals found in Zimbabwe
culturalNotes: Many Shona clans (madzinza) are named after animals — these are totems
The fish eagle and elephant are important national symbols

lessons.title: Zvisikwa — Nature
lessons.description: Learn words for the natural world — sky, water, mountains
culturalNotes: Nature is deeply respected in Shona culture
Many sacred places are found in natural settings like mountains and rivers

lessons.title: Kurwara neKupora — Health
lessons.description: Learn essential health vocabulary for visiting the doctor
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Kurwara neKupora
culturalNotes: Both traditional healers (n'anga) and modern doctors are consulted
Health is often discussed using metaphors in Shona

lessons.title: Mamiriro eKunze — Weather
lessons.description: Talk about weather and seasons in Shona
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Mamiriro eKunze
culturalNotes: Farming depends on rain — weather is a frequent topic
The rainy season (November-March) is vital for agriculture

lessons.title: Muguta — In the City
lessons.description: Navigate urban Zimbabwe with city vocabulary
culturalNotes: Harare and Bulawayo are the major cities
Many people move between urban and rural homes

lessons.title: Tekinoroji — Technology
lessons.description: Learn technology words used in modern Zimbabwean life
culturalNotes: Mobile phones (runhare) have transformed communication in Zimbabwe
WhatsApp is the dominant messaging platform

lessons.title: Shandirai — Social Media
lessons.description: Learn social media and online communication vocabulary
culturalNotes: Zimbabwe has a vibrant online culture
Social media plays a key role in news and community organizing

lessons.title: Mitambo neVaraidzo — Entertainment
lessons.description: Talk about sports, music, and entertainment in Shona
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Mitambo neVaraidzo
culturalNotes: Football (soccer) is the most popular sport
Sungura and Chimurenga music are beloved genres

lessons.title: Nyika Yedu — Our Country
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary about Zimbabwe as a nation and its governance
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Nyika Yedu
culturalNotes: Zimbabwe means 'house of stone' from the Great Zimbabwe ruins
National pride is strongly expressed in Shona

lessons.title: Kodzero — Rights
lessons.description: Learn about rights, voting, and civic participation
culturalNotes: Zimbabwe gained independence in 1980
Civic participation is seen as both a right and responsibility

lessons.title: Nhoroondo — History
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary about Zimbabwe's rich history
culturalNotes: The Chimurenga wars are central to Zimbabwe's identity
Oral history (nhoroondo) preserves knowledge across generations

lessons.title: Zvemabhizinesi — Business
lessons.description: Learn business and economic vocabulary for the workplace
culturalNotes: Zimbabwe has a strong entrepreneurial culture
Informal trading is a major part of the economy

lessons.title: Pakutanga... — Connecting Ideas
lessons.description: Learn discourse markers to connect ideas and tell stories fluently
culturalNotes: Good storytelling (kutaura ngano) is a respected skill
Using connectors makes your Shona sound more fluent

lessons.title: Dai Ndaiziva — If I Knew
lessons.description: Learn conditional expressions — if, would, could, might
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Dai Ndaiziva
culturalNotes: Conditional forms show nuanced thinking in Shona
These expressions are common in storytelling and planning

lessons.title: Ndinofarira — Likes & Interests
lessons.description: Express preferences, desires, and interests
culturalNotes: Sharing interests builds social bonds
It's common to ask about hobbies when getting to know someone

lessons.title: Rugare neHondo — Peace & Conflict
lessons.description: Learn abstract concepts about peace, conflict, and resolution
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Rugare neHondo
culturalNotes: Peace-building (kuyanana) is deeply valued
Traditional courts (dare) resolve community conflicts

lessons.title: Mabwe — Great Zimbabwe
lessons.description: Learn about Zimbabwe's ancient heritage and archaeological wonders
culturalNotes: Great Zimbabwe is a UNESCO World Heritage Site
The stone ruins date back to the 11th century

lessons.title: Mhemberero — Celebrations
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary for festivals, celebrations, and ceremonies
culturalNotes: Celebrations often blend traditional and modern elements
Music, dance, and food are central to all celebrations

lessons.title: Utano Hwepfungwa — Wellbeing
lessons.description: Learn vocabulary about mental health and emotional wellbeing
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Utano Hwepfungwa
culturalNotes: Mental health awareness is growing in Zimbabwe
Traditional concepts of 'kugutsikana' (contentment) align with modern wellness

lessons.title: Kufambisa Nyika — Travel
lessons.description: Learn travel vocabulary for exploring Zimbabwe and beyond
discoveryElements: Explore vocabulary related to: Kufambisa Nyika
culturalNotes: Zimbabwe has world-famous destinations like Victoria Falls
Travel broadens understanding — 'kufamba kuziva' (to travel is to know)
